references.text: Malachi prophesies about sending a messenger before the Lord's face to clear the way, which is reflected in Jesus' sending of messengers ahead of him.
Jesus quotes the prophecy about the messenger sent ahead, using the expression 'before your face' (πρὸ προσώπου), the same expression used in Luke 9:52.
Jesus sends out messengers (the seventy) two by two ahead of him to every place he himself was going to come, a parallel to the sending of messengers in Luke 9:52.
The verse that follows tells us that the Samaritans did not receive Jesus because his face was set toward Jerusalem, providing context for why the messengers were sent ahead.
Jesus travels through Samaria and encounters resistance and tensions between Jews and Samaritans, which provides background for the Samaritans' attitude in Luke 9:52.
The background of the Samaritans' mixed religion and the opposition between them and the Jews explains why they were unwilling to receive Jesus who was on his way to Jerusalem.
The hostility between Samaritans and Jews is shown by the fact that the Samaritans opposed the rebuilding of the temple, providing historical background for the tensions in Luke 9:52.
